hypothesis: A LoRA adapter trained for one epoch should outperform the in-context baseline on the full-30 held-out set, because fine-tuning bakes task-specific question style into the weights rather than relying on prompt instructions at inference time.
technique: Single greedy on-device call using a LoRA adapter (epoch 1) fine-tuned on the target task; no retrieval or multi-call pipeline — the adapter's weights carry all the learned behaviour.
result: Scored 0.274 on the full-30 gate (0 wins / 0 ties / 29 losses vs Sonnet); specPass was high at 97% and atomicity reached 4, but spec, coverage, naturalness, and non-redundancy all sat at 3, keeping quality below parity. Despite the weak win-rate this was retained as the new best, establishing the epoch-1 adapter as the baseline to beat.
label: adapter_e1_full
